use_when: Need a stable full-story structure
Need setup, escalation, and payoff
Need a midpoint or major turn
avoid_when: The project is only a short conceptual fragment

use_when: The protagonist goes through visible trials
The story needs a transformational arc
Need clear goal-obstacle-result progression
Need the scene to directly move the story
avoid_when: Time needs to be compressed instead of played out

use_when: Need to compress time
Need to summarize repeated actions
avoid_when: A key conflict must happen on screen

use_when: Need a bridge between two stronger scenes
Need to move relationship or setting without heavy conflict
avoid_when: The story should enter conflict immediately

use_when: Past information changes the meaning of the present
The reveal has emotional or structural payoff
Need anticipation or fate pressure
Need a future image to frame the present
Need to compress a multi-step process
Need visible passage of effort or accumulation
avoid_when: The process only has one meaningful beat

use_when: Need to show practice, growth, preparation, or upgrade
avoid_when: There is no visible change across steps

use_when: Need to establish repetition before breaking it
Need contrast between routine and disruption
Need visible passage of time
Need an atmospheric time jump
avoid_when: The scene should preserve immediate tension

diagnostic_rules: If a scene ends without changing the situation, it is probably weak.
If exposition lasts longer than conflict, the story will flatten.
If every scene uses the same engine, pacing will feel monotone.
If the midpoint does not raise risk or change understanding, escalation is weak.
